issue_context.title: File sensor template / path options not visible/editable in the UI
issue_context.body: ### The problem with 2024.6 came the UI config flow for File integration. details see below issue we see is that in the more-info, or the config for the entity itself, those value_templates are lost, and we can not adjust them. all we get is this nice sensor more info: ### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue? 2024.6.0 ### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core? _No response_ ### What type of installation are you running? Home Assistant OS ### Integration causing the issue File ### Link to integration documentation on our website https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/file ### Diagnostics information _No response_ ### Example YAML snippet ```yaml sensor: - platform: file file_path: /config/logging/filed/filed_notifications.txt name: Filed notifications <<: &truncate_value value_template: > {% if value is not none %} {% if value|length < 255 %} {{value}} {% else %} Truncated: {{value|truncate(240,True, '')}} {% endif %} {% endif %} ``` ### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us? _No response_ ### Additional information new config flow gives us the full set of options, including the template: and we can simply drop in those file_path and template from the yaml config above. sensor does work as expected as is seen above. however the template is missing (it's not in the entity_registry either) ``` {"aliases":[],"area_id":null,"categories":{},"capabilities":null,"config_entry_id":"c4ac56c0190d80309c023f4a98320c05","device_class":null,"device_id":null,"disabled_by":null,"entity_category":null,"entity_id":"sensor.filed_notifications","hidden_by":null,"icon":null,"id":"92f117e98be9ad9f6c530b405a74fe10","has_entity_name":false,"labels":[],"name":null,"options":{"conversation":{"should_expose":false},"cloud.google_assistant":{"should_expose":false}},"original_device_class":null,"original_icon":"mdi:file","original_name":"Filed notifications","platform":"file","supported_features":0,"translation_key":null,"unique_id":"c4ac56c0190d80309c023f4a98320c05","previous_unique_id":null,"unit_of_measurement":null} ``` is limiting the ability to adjust the sensor entity, just as the missing path is. The File integration overview does list those: Thats not reachable from within the more-info though, which is where these options should be listed per entity?

Hi @Mariusthvdb 

It's not easy to read but I guess your feedback is that you want an option to be able to change the value template afterwards (config entry options)?

Should not be too much of an effort to fix and seems logical to do but I think you're mixing a bit with helpers where you can change those options from the entity itself.
File integration is not a helper and therefore it's config entry options will be managed from it's integration page.

thx, appreciate your feedback!

and, well, it depends on you pov;-)

I suppose that when a migration is made from yaml to UI (and for the sensors, this was unannounced/unexpected, only services where mentioned?) which imports our value_templates, it is important those value_templates should be at least visible, and yes preferably editable. Same goes for the path.

The only other option now would be to delete the entity and create a new one.

Usecase: I had some experimenting time to find the correct value_templates for the truncating, and in yaml it was as easy as editing the template and reload.
Suppose that more complex template would require even more work. So that template is very important.

Lastly, since the template nor the file path are in the entity_registry: how can we be sure this is still valid, and taken into account?

> File integration is not a helper and therefore it's config entry options will be managed from it's integration page.

ah yes, found them in the config_entries....

```
      {
        "data": {
          "value_template": "{% if value is not none %}\n  {% if value|length < 255 %} {{value}}\n  {% else %} Truncated: {{value|truncate(240,True, '')}}\n  {% endif %}\n{% endif %}\n",
          "platform": "sensor",
          "file_path": "/config/logging/filed/filed_notifications.txt",
          "name": "Filed notifications"
        },
        "disabled_by": null,
        "domain": "file",
        "entry_id": "c4ac56c0190d80309c023f4a98320c05",
        "minor_version": 1,
        "options": {},
        "pref_disable_new_entities": false,
        "pref_disable_polling": false,
        "source": "import",
        "title": "Filed notifications [/config/logging/filed/filed_notifications.txt]",
        "unique_id": null,
        "version": 1
      },
      {
```

Helper or not imo shouldnt matter: how else would we be able to edit those UI entities. Btw, a helper entity is an entity, so why make a distinction on that concept..


Anyways: long story short: 

> not be too much of an effort to fix 


yes please fix ;-)

I'm in the same boat as [Mariusthvdb](https://github.com/Mariusthvdb)

I am restructuring my filesystem (able to do this due to all the recent label additions to HA)

I was ...
1. Hoping to be able to edit the filepaths of my 22 file.notify entities
2. Really expecting to see the file path of the file.notify entity as an attribute of the entity so I could use it in a single script that manages my files.

FYI I have scripts that generate YAML configuration files that do things like 

1. write my recorder include/exclude entries based on labels. 
2. generate entire packages that create throttled sensors and place them in my configuration. 
3. write optimized jinja files based on labelling option in HASS

For all of these use cases I have to remove the first two lines (created by the file notify service) because the cause the YAML, JINJA and CSV files to become non-YAML, non-JINJA and non-CSV files.

I want to have access to the file_path (in core.config_entries) as an attribute of a file entity so can use it in these HA yaml scripts, pass it to a BASH script that cleans up the files, removes special markers I have to add to jinja (to prevent HA from rendering it) etc.

It would be a lot more simple if I could just pass the notify.entity_id to my HA script and know that it can work out everything from that one entity.

> I suppose that when a migration is made from yaml to UI (and for the sensors, this was unannounced/unexpected, only services where mentioned?) which imports our value_templates, it is important those value_templates should be at least visible, and yes preferably editable. Same goes for the path.

I don't understand why the value templates aren't visible or editable. I cannot verify whether the migration happened correctly, and I won't be able to make future changes (it seems I'd need to remove and re-add a particular configuration). Like Marius, I searched the internal storage files, but cannot find my existing value templates in there. Beats me where this is stored. What is the reasoning behind not making this visible and editable, or will there be an update to facilitate this?

Also, what is the default scan interval? 30 seconds? I'm assuming I need to switch this off and create automations for custom scan intervals, right?

EDIT: The reason I couldn't find it in `.storage` is due to a migration bug: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/119404.

Not being able to see or edit the value templates would be a show-stopper for me updating to 2024.6.x.

Obviously that's a pretty important thing to verify, and one which often needs to be tweaked before getting it right.

If that's not possible, then please add me to the list of users respectfully requesting that it be added. Or maybe I'm misunderstanding, since I haven't updated yet and can't see this first hand.

I'd appreciate to be at least able to see the filename which was given while creating the notification via the File Integration. Otherwise debugging will be quite hard.
tia
Andy
